structure.overview: This case concerns an appeal by Eli Lilly Canada Inc. (appellants) against Mylan Pharmaceuticals ULC (respondent) regarding the admissibility of a UK patent in appeal materials. Mylan moved to preclude Eli Lilly from referring to the UK patent, arguing it is not a legal authority or regulation under Canadian law. The Federal Court of Appeal partially granted the motion, ruling that direct reference to the UK patent is not permitted but allowing the appellants to highlight UK court decisions and related patent portions to the hearing panel, which has discretion over evidence.

party_points.text: Move to preclude appellants from referring to UK patent
Refer to UK patent citing UK House of Lords decision
UK patent not authority or regulation under Canadian law
UK patent is authority, no fresh evidence motion needed; alternatively, admissibility left to hearing panel

left_open.text: Appellants must move to admit UK patent as fresh evidence under Rule 351, not before court now
Appellants may highlight UK court decisions and patent portions to hearing panel
Hearing panel has discretion to allow evidence; its decision prevails over motions judge

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Respondent Mylan moves to preclude appellants from referring to the UK patent in their appeal materials and before the panel.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Appellants refer to the UK patent in their memorandum citing a UK House of Lords decision approved by Rothstein J. in Sanofi.

citations.why: Appellants rely on Sanofi quoting UK House of Lords decision

citations.cite: Du Pont de Nemours (Witsiepe’s) Application [1982] FSR 303, HL
citations.why: Appellants rely on UK House of Lords decision Witsiepe’s

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Respondent argues the UK patent is not an authority or regulation under Federal Courts Rules or Interpretation Act and is evidence not before the Federal Court.

citations.cite: Rules 348(1) and 70(1)(e) of the Federal Courts Rules, S.O.R./98-106
citations.why: Respondent argues UK patent is not an authority under these rules

citations.cite: subsections 2(1), 3(1), and 35(1) of the Interpretation Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. I-21
citations.why: Respondent argues UK patent is not a regulation under these provisions

citations.cite: Rule 351 of the Federal Courts Rules
citations.why: Respondent says UK patent can only be presented via fresh evidence motion under this rule

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Appellants argue UK patent is an authority as cited by House of Lords in Supreme Court decision and relates to law, so no fresh evidence motion needed; alternatively, admissibility should be left to hearing panel.
idea_list: Admissibility better left to hearing panel

citations.cite: Apotex Inc. v. Sanofi-Synthelabo Canada Inc., 2008 SCC 61, [2008] 3 S.C.R. 265 (Sanofi)
citations.why: Appellants rely on Sanofi to support UK patent as authority

citations.cite: Eli Lilly Canada Inc. v. Novopharm Limited, 2010 FCA 130, 2010 CarswellNat 1424 at para. 10 (Novopharm)
citations.why: Appellants rely on Novopharm to argue admissibility should be left to panel

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court will first address the appellants' argument that admissibility should be left to the hearing panel.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court prefers to decide the admissibility of the UK patent now to provide certainty and finds Novopharm inapplicable as no hearing date is set.

citations.why: Novopharm deferred admissibility to panel because hearing was imminent, unlike here

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds direct reference to the UK patent is not permitted for three reasons.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: First, appellants ask the court to accept UK patent evidence from UK first instance court and draw conclusions, which is improper.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The UK patent remains evidence in UK and Canadian courts and does not become law simply because construed by a court; Parliament requires foreign patents be admitted as evidence.

citations.cite: Section 14 of the Patent Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. P-4
citations.why: Parliament requires foreign patents be admitted as evidence by certified copy

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: A case's legal principle is limited to its proven facts; Lord Halsbury's 120-year-old statement confirms judgments apply only to their facts.

citations.cite: Quinn v. Leathem, [1901] A.C. (H.L.) 495 at page 81
citations.why: Confirms judgments apply only to particular facts proved

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Appellants' argument blurs the distinction between facts and law, merging evidence and law improperly.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Second, Federal Courts Rules require authorities to be legal sources, which a patent is not; courts are cautious about admitting evidence as legislative facts.

citations.cite: Rules 70(1)(e) and 348(1) of the Federal Courts Rules
citations.why: Defines authorities as statutes, jurisprudence, or legal writings

citations.cite: AstraZeneca Canada Inc. v. Apotex Inc., 2003 FCA 487, [2004] 2 F.C.R. 364 at paras. 6-11
Public School Boards' Assn. (Alberta) v. Alberta (Attorney General), 2000 SCC 2, [2000] 1 S.C.R. 44
citations.why: Courts cautious about admitting evidence as legislative facts

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Third, appellants' argument that the UK patent is a regulation fails because the Interpretation Act's definition applies only to Canadian patents.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Interpretation Act defines regulation as letters patent under Canadian authority, not foreign legislation or sovereign authority.

citations.why: Defines regulation as letters patent under Canadian authority

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: In sum, a foreign patent is not an authority recognized by this Court.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The court introduces three closing observations.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: First, the UK patent was not admitted in Federal Court trial; appellants must move to admit it as fresh evidence under Rule 351, which is not before the court now.

citations.why: Fresh evidence on appeal requires motion under Rule 351

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Second, appellants may highlight UK court decisions and related patent portions to the hearing panel to support their position.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Third, the hearing panel has discretion to allow evidence and documents, and its decision prevails over a motions judge's ruling; thus, the court declines to preclude the patent before the panel.

citations.cite: Sport Maska Inc. v. Bauer Hockey Corp., 2016 FCA 44, [2016] 4 F.C.R. 3 at para. 37
citations.why: Panel decision has precedence over motions judge

citations.cite: Apotex Inc. v. Canada (Health), 2017 FCA 160, 36 Admin. L.R. (6th) 110 at para. 16
citations.why: Panel has discretion to receive evidence

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court grants the motion in part, fixes costs at $5,000, and signs the order.
